questions.questionText: How does spear phishing differ from generic mass phishing?

options.text: Spear phishing is automated using pop-up advertisements
Spear phishing is highly targeted at a specific individual or team using researched details
Spear phishing only targets mobile phones using text messages
Spear phishing requires physical entry into an office building

questions.explanation: Spear phishing relies on prior reconnaissance to tailor realistic messages directly to specific targets.

questions.questionText: What does the acronym "OSINT" stand for in cybersecurity reconnaissance?

options.text: Operational System Internal Network Tracking
Open Source Intelligence
Optical Security Inspection for Network Traffic
Offline Storage Integration and Networking Tool

questions.explanation: OSINT stands for Open Source Intelligence, referring to publicly available data mined from social platforms, repositories, and directories.

questions.questionText: Public professional profiles on LinkedIn can provide attackers with information used to craft spear phishing messages.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: True. Attackers mine job titles, reporting structures, vendor software, and current projects from LinkedIn profiles to build convincing pretexts.

questions.questionText: Why do attackers often send password-protected .zip files containing malicious attachments?

options.text: To save hard drive storage space on remote laptops
To prevent email security gateways from scanning the encrypted contents for malware
To make the file download faster over home Wi-Fi networks
Because password protection automatically executes scripts

questions.explanation: Email gateway scanners cannot inspect encrypted archive contents without the password, allowing malicious payloads past boundary defenses.

questions.questionText: Enabling macros on an unverified Microsoft Word or Excel attachment is safe as long as the document has a .docm extension.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: False. The .docm extension explicitly denotes a macro-enabled document. Enabling macros runs underlying VBA code that can install malware. #### **Medium Level (Questions 6–13)**

questions.questionText: Which public sources are commonly harvested by adversaries during the OSINT phase of a spear phishing campaign? (Select ALL that apply)

options.text: LinkedIn corporate organizational charts
Public GitHub code repositories detailing software libraries
Personal social media posts detailing travel or conference attendance
Encrypted database servers operating behind private firewalls

questions.explanation: LinkedIn, GitHub, and social media posts provide open public data. Private encrypted database servers are not public OSINT sources.

questions.questionText: You are a remote graphic designer. You receive a direct message on Telegram from someone claiming to be a senior manager at your main client account, asking you to open Design_Brief.pdf.exe. How should you react?

options.text: Open the file immediately since it contains "pdf" in the filename
Do not open the file; the double extension (.pdf.exe) indicates an executable file
Rename the file to .doc and then double-click it
Forward the file to a friend on personal social media

questions.explanation: Files ending in .exe are executable programs. The .pdf.exe naming convention tricks users into opening executable malware.

questions.questionText: Spear phishing attempts only target executive leadership (CEOs/CFOs), never entry-level remote contractors or virtual assistants.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: False. Attackers regularly target contractors, virtual assistants, and junior personnel as initial footholds to access corporate networks or facilitate payment fraud.

questions.questionText: What operating system settings and user habits help defend against weaponized spear phishing attachments? (Select ALL that apply)

options.text: Disabling "Hide extensions for known file types" in OS file settings
Keeping Microsoft Office "Block macros from running in Office files from the Internet" enabled
Always opening untrusted email attachments using Administrator rights
Verifying unexpected file transfers with the sender via an independent communication channel

questions.explanation: Revealing full file extensions, blocking Office macros, and out-of-band verification mitigate attachment risks. Running untrusted files as Administrator increases security risks.

questions.questionText: A spear phisher notices on Twitter that your company’s Lead Developer is on a 14-hour flight. The attacker emails you posing as the Lead Developer, requesting emergency production database credentials. Should you comply?

options.text: True (Comply immediately)
False (Do not comply)

questions.explanation: False. Attackers exploit travel schedules to create situations where the spoofed identity cannot be reached easily. Always follow established verification protocols.

questions.questionText: What technical feature makes MITRE ATT&CK Technique T1566.001 particularly dangerous to enterprise endpoint security?

options.text: It uses physical USB drives dropped in parking lots
It relies on user execution of attached files to run malware inside the local user environment
It automatically changes home router DNS addresses without user interaction
It turns off laptop Wi-Fi adapters permanently

questions.explanation: Technique T1566.001 relies on social engineering to trick the user into executing malicious attachments locally.

questions.questionText: Reducing the amount of detailed operational information shared on public social media accounts helps reduce your exposure to OSINT reconnaissance.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: True. Practicing digital footprint hygiene limits the intelligence attackers can use to build spear phishing lures.

questions.questionText: Spear phishers only target executives; entry-level remote contractors are never targeted because they lack system permissions.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Entry-level contractors are frequently targeted as initial access points to pivot deeper into enterprise networks or harvest credentials.

questions.questionText: Which of the following indicate that a project brief attachment might be a spear-phishing payload? *(Select TWO)*

options.text: The attachment is a .pdf file under 500 KB.
The attachment is an .xlsm file requiring macro activation to view text.
The file name ends in .docx.iso.
The file was downloaded directly from the company's official Google Drive.

questions.explanation: Macro-enabled files (.xlsm) and disk image archives (.iso) disguised as documents are common malicious delivery formats.

questions.questionText: What information can an attacker gather from your public GitHub profile to make a spear-phishing email believable?

options.text: Your private home Wi-Fi password
Programming languages used, active repositories, and collaborator usernames
Your hardware MFA seed keys
Your credit card PIN

questions.explanation: Public GitHub repositories display technical environments, active projects, and peer collaborators.

questions.questionText: A freelancer receives a high-paying offer on Upwork. The client insists on sending an .iso file containing "project assets" before contract signing. Why is this suspicious?

options.text: .iso files are standard image files that cannot contain text.
An .iso file is a disk image that can bypass basic scanner checks and mount an executable drive on Windows/Mac.
Freelancers are legally prohibited from receiving .iso files.
.iso files automatically delete the operating system upon opening.

questions.explanation: ISO files are container formats used by attackers to deliver malware while evading basic security filters.

questions.questionText: Spear phishing relies solely on technical software exploits and does not use psychological manipulation.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Spear phishing is a socio-technical attack combining technical delivery vectors with psychological manipulation (trust, urgency, authority).

questions.questionText: What step should you take before opening a password-protected .zip file from an external party?

options.text: Open it on a personal device to protect work systems.
Verify the source out-of-band and inspect unzipped contents in an isolated environment or sandbox.
Forward the password to your bank.
Disable your endpoint firewall.

questions.explanation: Verifying the source through another channel and inspecting files securely prevents payload execution.

questions.questionText: What term describes altering sender details so an email appears to come from a legitimate internal colleague?

options.text: Port forwarding
Email Header Spoofing
Hard drive partitioning
Disk defragmentation

questions.explanation: Email spoofing manipulates header fields (From:) to impersonate legitimate contacts.

questions.questionText: An email claiming to be from your company's HR department contains a link to "Updated W-2 Tax Forms." The link URL points to http://hr-portal.tax-verify-auth.com. What is the safest course of action?

options.text: Click the link and enter your Social Security Number.
Hover over the link, identify the external domain, do not click, and report it to security/HR.
Email your password to HR to check for you.
Ignore all future HR emails forever.

questions.explanation: Identifying external, non-company domain names by hovering over links helps detect phishing portals before entering credentials. MODULE 3: Smishing
